items.title: [CI] Flaky tests and CI infrastructure failures seen while babysitting PRs
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

<!-- sglang-flaky-tracker:v1 -->

This issue tracks **flaky tests** and **recurring CI infrastructure failures** seen in NVIDIA `PR Test Base` / `PR Test Extra` runs while babysitting PRs with the `/sglang-pr-babysit` Claude Code workflow. It complements the CI tracker #17050. #17050 lists every failure signature by date. This issue records one row per flaky test, how often it was hit, and whether a rerun with no code change passed. Use it to pick the flakiest tests to debug.

A row is added only when triage found concrete evidence that the failure is **not caused by the PR** and **not a breakage on `main`**. PR-caused failures, `main` breakages, and uncertain cases are left out. Jobs that `github-actions[bot]` cancelled during a run of the maintainers' [Cancel Unfinished PR Runs](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/workflows/cancel-unfinished-pr-tests.yml) workflow are also left out. Those are deliberate cancels, not flakes or infrastructure failures.

## Format (v1)

Each row is one failure mode, keyed by **Test** (or **Job / step**) plus **Signature**. The same test failing with a different signature gets its own row.

- **ID**: `T<n>` for tests and `I<n>` for infra. IDs are never reused, even when a row is fixed or removed. Retired IDs: `I2`-`I10` (removed on 2026-10-08 because they were `Cancel Unfinished PR Runs` cancels).
- **Test**: `path::Class::method`, with the path relative to the repo root. Use `path` alone if the method is unknown.
- **Job / step**: the workflow job name, a slash, and the failing step or action.
- **Signature**: the exception type and message, with run-specific values (numbers, paths, hashes, ports, timestamps) replaced by `<N>`, `<PATH>`, and so on. At most about 100 characters.
- **Runner**: the runner label of the failing job, for example `1-gpu-h100` or `8-gpu-b300`.
- **Seen**: the number of failed job attempts recorded. Each failed attempt counts once, including a failed rerun.
- **Rerun passed**: `P/R`. `R` is the number of occurrences whose rerun has finished. `P` is how many of those reruns passed the same job with no code change.
- **First seen** / **Last seen**: UTC dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Recent jobs**: links to the last 3 failing jobs, newest first. Each link is labeled with its PR number.
- **Status**: `open`; `investigating (@user or #issue)`; or `fixed (#PR)`. If a `fixed` row fails again after the fix merged, it returns to `open` with `regressed after #PR`.

Rows are sorted by **Seen**, highest first. Ties are broken by **Last seen**, newest first.

Every occurrence is also posted as a comment on this issue. The comment starts with `<!-- sglang-flaky-occurrence:v1 -->` and holds the entry ID, PR, job link, why the failure is unrelated to the PR, and the rerun result. The comments are the append-only record, and the tables above are their summary.

## For debugging agents

Start from the top of each table. A test row with a high **Seen** count and a high **Rerun passed** ratio is a confirmed flake, and it is worth fixing or stabilizing. When you take a row, set its **Status** to `investigating (@you)`. When the fix merges, set it to `fixed (#PR)`.

## Motivation

Add deepseek_v4_flash 1p1d accuracy case and register it to the nightly pipeline

## Modifications

1. Add accuracy test case test/registered/npu/accuracy/deepseek_v4_flash/test_npu_deepseek_v4_flash_0731_w8a8_1p1d_16p_gpqa.py :

- Implement a multi-node PD-Sep accuracy test based on TestNpuAccuracyMultiNodePdSepTestCaseBase , reusing DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_0731_W8A8_MODEL_PATH from test_npu_performance_utils .
- Define the full PD-Sep deployment configuration:
  - Environment variables : common envs (including DSPARK/Spec V2, DeepEP, and HCCL related settings), plus node-specific overrides for Prefill ( HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2048 , long-sequence DeepEP parameters, etc.) and Decode ( HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1200 , SGLANG_NPU_SPLIT_SHARED_EXPERT_OVERLAP=1 , etc.).
  - Prefill node launch arguments : TP16/DP16, dsv4 attention backend, DeepEP normal mode, modelslim quantization, --disaggregation-mode prefill , Ascend transfer backend, --mem-fraction-static 0.68 , CUDA Graph disabled.
  - Decode node launch arguments : TP16/DP16, DeepEP low_latency mode, --disaggregation-mode decode , CUDA Graph decode batch sizes 1–10, DSPARK speculative decoding enabled ( --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 , with a W8A8-quantized draft model).
  - Router arguments : --policy cache_aware .
- Add test class TestNPUDeepSeekV4Flash0731W8A8PDSEPGPQAHigh , evaluating the gpqa_diamond dataset with accuracy baseline 0.874, eval batch size 128, and generation config for Think High mode ( thinking=True , reasoning_effort=high , max_tokens=125000 ).
- Register the case via register_npu_ci as a nightly test (est_time=3600, currently marked disabled="accuracy testcase" ).
2. Update nightly pipeline .github/workflows/nightly-test-npu.yml :

- Add a new deepseek_v4_flash_w8a8_1p1d_16p accuracy test entry to the multi-node test matrix (prefill_size=1, decode_size=1, router_size=1, test_type: 'accuracy' , PD separation deployment), pointing to the new test case and integrating it into the nightly NPU e2e multi-node workflow.

items.body: ## Motivation Currently, `AscendAttnBackend` inherits `needs_cpu_seq_lens=True`. items.title: [Feat] [NPU] dwdp: support DWDP on Ascend NPU
items.body:
## Motivation

Enable `--dwdp-size` on Ascend NPU using the existing GPU DWDP algorithm from #29778.

DWDP keeps each rank's tokens local and prefetches peer expert weights into two reusable buffer slots. This targets MoE prefill, especially disaggregated prefill workers; it is not intended to improve integrated decode throughput.

## Modifications

- Share `DwdpManager`, `DWDPTransport`, `WeightBuffer`, `PagePool` and `DWDPWeightManager` between GPU and NPU. Layer discovery, expert ownership, page layout, remote-slice copies and double-buffer stream/event scheduling reuse the existing implementation.
- Add a thin NPU backend in `hardware_backend/npu/dwdp/vmm.py` for ACL VMM operations, NZ-to-ND weight migration, pointer-backed NPU tensors, ACL V2 FABRIC handle exchange with PID authorization, and resource cleanup.
- Keep local expert shards resident. Reuse fixed-size pages for the two remote-weight slots and copy all remote expert slices on each forward, including boundary bytes. Cache device selection during initialization.
- Preserve the GPU allocation, FABRIC/POSIX-FD selection and driver-call ordering. NPU uses FABRIC only, without an ACL IPC fallback. Initialization collectives are separate from local migration-error collection; imported mappings are released before local physical memory, with stepwise release bookkeeping.
- Preserve existing common model/configuration checks, graph policy and user/model shared-expert settings. No model-specific, Attention, ordinary EP, DeepEP or FuseEP changes are included. Existing upstream GPU DWDP tests are unchanged; no test or documentation files are added by this PR.

Current diff: **6 production files, +526/-112** relative to `889658a5be0331a23794eb43ab7fa6421029d651`.

## Accuracy Tests

### Current revision

Head: `1e87eb7993b02669053e8e4e34c97afeb4c6c542`.

**The latest shared-lifecycle refactor has only been statically checked. Model accuracy, real-device operation, performance and graph replay have not been rerun for this head. Historical results below are not validation of the current revision.**

Passed: isort 7.0.0, Ruff 0.15.1 formatting and selected lint checks, Python syntax compilation, and `git diff --check`. Source/AST review confirmed unchanged GPU driver-call and runtime prefetch-call ordering; this is not a hardware regression test.

### Historical model accuracy

Model: `Qwen3-30B-A3B-W8A8`. CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post6. Same 200 GSM8K examples, 5-shot completion prompts, concurrency 8, temperature 0, top_p 1, maximum 512 output tokens; cache flushed before evaluation.

| Mode | Correct / 200 | Accuracy | Failed | Length-limited | Evaluation time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP8 + attention DP8, EP1 | 184 | 92% | 0 | 0 | 111.05 s |
| Ordinary EP8 + attention DP8* | 186 | 93% | 0 | 0 | 105.78 s |
| DWDP8 + attention DP8 | 186 | 93% | 0 | 6 | 1041.80 s |

These single-host results were collected on 2026-10-06, before the shared-copy refactor, using the earlier ACL IPC implementation. ACL IPC is **not** included in this PR. The substantially longer DWDP evaluation time reflects its per-forward weight transfer cost during decode.

*The ordinary EP row used separate experimental routing/combine fixes outside this PR and is provided only as a reference.

<details>
<summary>Historical FABRIC and operator validation</summary>

- At `786b95edc32c880bc52b2eeb012f76516861b1be`, six real two-NPU MoE cases passed: BF16/FP16/INT8 with small and large weights. Coverage included FABRIC setup, ND/NZ migration, MoE output parity, fixed-page reuse across different layer widths, remote-weight poisoning/restoration including boundaries, local-shard preservation, unequal forward counts, and repeated cleanup.
- At `fe830622abef6736651b5ce96cb5893325946cce`, two hosts with one NPU each passed real FABRIC export, PID authorization, import, mapping, and three exact bidirectional copies of 4,194,338 bytes per direction per round. The earlier two-host DWDP2 run of the same model completed 200/200 GSM8K requests, with 184 correct (92%) and no failed requests.

These earlier revisions predate the current shared lifecycle and do not establish current-head or A5 cross-host support.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Historical prefill benchmark

Same model and earlier single-host checkout as the accuracy table. **128 total requests, client/server concurrency 8**, 8192 input tokens and 1 output token per request. Attention TP1, eager prefill, seed 1, `max-total-tokens=32768`, radix cache disabled. Each server received 128 warmup requests, then a cache flush and 128 measured requests. All rounds completed 128/128.

| Mode | NPUs | Input tokens/s | Duration | Mean TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP2 + attention DP2, EP1 | 2 | 14,896.28 | 70.39 s | 4.154 s |
| TP4 + attention DP4, EP1 | 4 | 23,895.56 | 43.88 s | 2.594 s |
| TP8 + attention DP8, EP1 | 8 | 33,027.27 | 31.75 s | 1.899 s |
| Ordinary EP8 + attention DP8* | 8 | 25,380.01 | 41.32 s | 2.465 s |
| DWDP8 + attention DP8 | 8 | 73,758.27 | 14.22 s | 0.847 s |

Single measured rounds, not repeated statistical measurements or current-head performance results. These are prefill measurements, not end-to-end decode speedups. The ordinary EP caveat above also applies here. No profiling result is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Historical DeepEP tuning reference (DWDP disabled)</summary>

At `e754adf1b06b507a9772fab5006aa7d2d083d27e` on 2026-10-08, the same model and workload were measured on eight NPUs without separate EP fixes. After 128 warmup requests, three rounds were measured with a flush before each; the same 200 GSM8K examples were evaluated after another flush.

| Existing DeepEP configuration | Input tokens/s, three rounds | Median | GSM8K |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Dispatch 512 tokens x 64 rounds, long-sequence combine | 14,454.59 / 14,604.09 / 13,871.11 | 14,454.59 | 184/200 (92%) |
| Dispatch 2048 tokens x 16 rounds, single-round combine | 24,876.21 / 25,005.84 / 25,107.09 | 25,005.84 | 182/200 (91%) |

Both completed 200/200 with no failed requests; length-limited responses were 0 and 2. This is a reference for existing DeepEP tuning, not a DWDP implementation change. Single-round combine was validated only up to 8192 local prefill tokens/rank. Other NPUs on the host were not fully isolated.

</details>

## Scope and Limitations

- FABRIC requires compatible hardware, CANN, drivers and topology, including for single-host jobs. Unsupported environments fail; there is no alternate transport fallback. Export success alone does not establish cross-host mapping or copying support. A5 cross-host operation is not claimed.
- Common DWDP topology restrictions remain: DWDP=TP=EP, attention DP=DWDP, MoE TP1, PP1, and a uniform routed-expert count divisible by DWDP size.
- Graphs remain disabled by default, with the existing common configuration precedence. No new graph, shared-expert, LoRA/PDMux, offload or memory-saver support is claimed by preserving the common argument policy.
- Historical NPU operator coverage includes BF16/FP16 and W8A8 INT8; it does not establish blanket compatibility with other quantization layouts or kernels.
- General distributed failure recovery and setup retry after destructive weight migration are not provided.

Current-head functional, accuracy and performance regression testing remains pending. Static checks do not establish that CI or merge requirements are satisfied.

## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash is a Z.ai hybrid-attention MoE VLM that interleaves MLA + DSA
(DeepSeek Sparse Attention) with linear attention and ships a built-in MTP head
for NEXTN speculative decoding. This PR ports the Ascend NPU adaptation
(Atlas A3/A5, developed on an internal fork, commits 1c76e6a01d..47594f8e1)
onto current upstream main (8854857a99), so the model can be served with SGLang
on Ascend clusters with PD disaggregation and speculative decoding.

## Modifications

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.

Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

Co-authors: @jychen21 @AichenF
Submitted by: @GnohzZ 

> **Draft / dependency scope:** this is opt-in, experimental SM120 support requiring a FlashInfer source build containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6346 (validated at `399b6c1d31a13f38dd827018f89c6a04c8487acb`). The default FlashInfer `0.7.1` pin and Docker/CI dependencies remain unchanged. An older build gives an explicit startup error only when SM120 MegaMoE is selected; the regular SM120 backend remains available. The cookbook includes a fixed-revision source-install recipe. We propose reviewing this guarded integration ahead of a dependency release; out-of-box support and validation against a released dependency will follow a coordinated version bump. The candidate is rebased onto main `2528cd2b91`, including CI maintenance base `ff8d964cf5b6`.

## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` currently requires SM100. FlashInfer #6346 added `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake`, a fused EP all-to-all + MXFP4 x MXFP8 expert-compute kernel for SM120 (RTX PRO Blackwell) that runs through the same `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer` API this backend already uses. This PR wires it into the existing `flashinfer_megamoe` path for FP4-expert checkpoints, starting with DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

The kernel targets **prefill**. On 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (72 GB, PCIe) it roughly doubles prefill throughput over `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` at the same TP4 / attention-DP4 layout, while decode with a few requests per rank is slower (numbers below). The recommended use is the prefill server of a PD-disaggregated deployment, with decode on the existing SM120 recipe; the server logs this at startup when it is not a PD prefill server.

The PR also fixes a static-EPLB bug on DeepSeek's `forward_normal` path, which serves `flashinfer_megamoe` (SM100 included) and the plain TP MoE: it only mapped logical to physical expert ids with `--enable-eplb`, so `--init-expert-location` alone (which also selects a dispatch algorithm) left the router's logical ids pointing at the physical layout the weights were loaded in.

## Modifications

1. **[Fix] `models/deepseek_v2.py`**: `DeepseekV2MoE._normal_path_dispatch_info()` always builds `ExpertLocationDispatchInfo` on non-NextN layers, as the DeepEP path already does. `init_new` returns `None` without a dispatch algorithm, so the default path is unchanged.
2. **SM120 branch of `flashinfer_megamoe`** (`layers/moe/flashinfer_megamoe.py`, `arg_groups/moe_hook.py`, `environ.py`):
   - Platform gate: SM120 with compute capability exactly 12.0, FP4 experts, EP >= 2, and a FlashInfer build exporting `Sm120_Mxfp4_Mxfp8_Bf16_Cake_MegaMoeConfig` (clear error otherwise). `--enable-eplb` is rejected (the packed scales are not expert-major); speculative decoding without an explicit `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` is rejected (the default draft runner `flashinfer_trtllm` is SM100-only). Settings the SM120 kernel cannot honor fail at startup instead of after the model loads: an unknown transport table, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`, the SM100-only `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_COMBINE_DTYPE` / `..._IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE`, and a per-rank prefill chunk or CUDA-graph batch larger than the workspace (`validate_flashinfer_megamoe_sm120_token_budget`). SM100 behaviour is unchanged.
   - `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` by default on this path: the kernel joins the EP group's NCCL communicator through NCCL's Device API, which needs cuMem buffers (SGLang otherwise sets it to 0). Same pattern as the `deepep_v2` branch.
   - Weights: FlashInfer's own preprocessing (`preprocess_sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_cake_mega_weights`). FC1 is a gate/up row interleave of `w13` and is written back into `w13`; FC1/FC2 alias the layer weights, so the experts stay resident once. The float32 (E8M0-widened) checkpoint scales are converted exactly to UE8M0 bytes and replaced by the packed kernel scales.
   - Forward: one pooled workspace; each call stages `compile_tokens_per_rank = max(get_dp_global_num_tokens())`, identical on every EP rank, so there is no per-layer routing all-gather / host sync, and each decode CUDA-graph batch size captures its own bucket. `MegaMoeTunedForward` is not used on SM120 (it would build one compiled kernel + NCCL window set per profiled capacity). Router ids are widened to int64 for this kernel. The kernel's `protocol_error` flag (BF16 return-codec overflow) is not read on the hot path because that needs a host sync; the default codec reserve is 25 % of a row, real V4-Flash activations need about 0.3 %.
   - `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` (default `lsa_where_reachable`) selects the peer transport.
3. **Tests** (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): `test_flashinfer_megamoe.py` (bucket = max over DP ranks + int64 ids, cake config / no startup tuning, swiglu limit, exact UE8M0 conversion, single resident copy of the experts), `test_server_args.py` (SM120 accept / reject cases, cuMem default, token budget), new `test_deepseek_moe_dispatch_info.py` (both real normal-forward entrypoints exercise physical expert selection without `--enable-eplb`; both fail with the pre-fix bodies, while no-dispatch and NextN controls pass); `test/manual/dsv4/test_sm120_flash.py` runs the cookbook recipe on four SM120 GPUs (sgl-eval GSM8K smoke and AIME25).
4. **Docs**: DeepSeek-V4 cookbook, new "FlashInfer MegaMoE on SM120 for prefill (Experimental)" note.

**Local CPU validation** on the rebased candidate: server-args, FlashInfer MegaMoE, EPLB and normal-forward dispatch suites: 376 passed, 1 skipped; pre-commit passed for all changed files. A cake server smoke also passed on the rebased candidate using FlashInfer source `399b6c1d`; validation against the eventual released dependency remains pending.

**Test environment** (GPU numbers below, collected before the rebase): one host, 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (SM120, PCIe, two CPU sockets), driver 580.95.05; image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` built 2026-10-13 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0) with this branch on top of `27b68303d0` and FlashInfer main `399b6c1d` (#6346) from source; model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`; sgl-eval 0.1.2. Unless noted: `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4` on GPUs 0-3.

**Dependency compatibility (2026-10-16).** With the actual installed FlashInfer `0.7.1` wheel (module loaded from `site-packages`, no source override), server-args, MegaMoE adapter and expert-remapping CPU suites passed: 334 tests and 140 subtests. A separate CPU probe uses real FlashInfer imports and simulated SM120 platform facts: default/`flashinfer_mxfp4` argument processing succeeds, while explicit SM120 MegaMoE selection raises the expected missing-backend error. This probe does not claim GPU execution. The existing unit test also covers a missing cake API.

The fixed source revision was additionally installed as an editable package (`0.7.2+g399b6c1d`) in the pinned CUDA 13 image, without a `PYTHONPATH` overlay or disabled version checks. Runtime and distribution versions match, the recorded Git commit matches, and the same 334 tests / 140 subtests pass. Old cubin/JIT-cache distributions and their orphan namespace directories were removed; the source build validates its kernel manifest. This installation intentionally overrides SGLang's `0.7.1` pin (`pip check` reports that mismatch), and ordinary default-wheel CI does not exercise the new cake kernel.

The actual released-wheel GPU check also passed on 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP4/attention-DP4 and `flashinfer_mxfp4`: four HTTP chat requests completed with nonempty responses, including correct answers to 17 x 23 and 48 + 24. FlashInfer autotune logs identify version `0.7.1`; the container had an empty `PYTHONPATH` and no version-check bypass. This is a functional smoke, not an accuracy benchmark.

The source-installed cake GPU smoke also passed on the same GPUs/model/parallelism, using the separately built image and a fresh JIT workspace: all four requests completed, arithmetic checks returned 391 and 72, and server logs identify `0.7.2+g399b6c1d`. The smoke exercised eager prefill plus decode CUDA Graph capture/replay; generated cake binding/device artifacts are present under that version's cache. This validates the source-install recipe without changing the previously reported accuracy/performance measurements.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731), 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (PCIe), `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4`.

**GSM8K-1319** (`sgl-eval run gsm8k --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, sgl-eval 0.1.2: the model's preset, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max):

| config | score | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` (baseline) | 96.59 % | 0 % | 0 % |
| `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` (this PR) | 96.13 % | 0 % | 0 % |

**GPQA-diamond** (`sgl-eval run gpqa --from-dataset <gpqa_diamond.jsonl> --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --n-repeats 4`, sgl-eval 0.1.2, 198 questions x 4 repeats). Both arms used the model preset: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max, and `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": true}`.

| config | pass@1 (avg of 4) | repeat-level SEM | pass@4 | majority@4 | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_mxfp4` | 90.28 % | 0.56 % | 93.94 % | 90.15 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |
| `flashinfer_megamoe` | 90.15 % | 0.44 % | 93.94 % | 90.66 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |

These results replace the earlier temperature-0 / 32k-cap run. Scores were independently recomputed from all 792 outputs per arm. The SEM is across four repeats of the same 198 questions; it is not a confidence interval over independently sampled questions or a formal equivalence test.

**AIME25** (`test/manual/dsv4/test_sm120_flash.py::TestSM120FlashFlashInferMegaMoE::test_aime25`, the fixture shared with the other DeepSeek-V4 cookbook tests: sgl-eval, 30 x 16 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, `--max-tokens 65536`): pass@1 = 98.1 % (SEM 0.5 %), pass@16 = 100 %, no truncation, threshold 0.93. `test_smoke_gsm8k` of the same file passes as well.

**Static EPLB** (a recording of V4-Flash routing, `--init-expert-location <file> --ep-dispatch-algorithm static`, no `--enable-eplb`) on this PR's backend; GSM8K-200 via the deprecated `sglang.test.run_eval` (5-shot), run before upstream moved to sgl-eval:

| config | GSM8K-200 | pf1k input tok/s | ShareGPT input tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, no EPLB | 0.990 | 26109 | 1561 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 0 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25013 | 1507 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 32 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25633 | 1453 |
| recorded placement, 0 redundant, **without the EPLB fix** (commit 1 reverted) | 0.005 (garbled output) | 25152 | 1587 |

(The no-EPLB reference is the median of three c1 rounds; the recorded-placement rows are single c3 rounds. They demonstrate functional correctness, but are not a controlled estimate of remapping overhead.)

The same bug on the plain TP MoE path (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, no a2a backend, `--init-expert-location <file>` only, which selects the `dynamic` dispatch algorithm): GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) = 0.0 % on the base commit, 96.5 % with commit 1.

**PD-disaggregated functional check** (cake prefill server on GPUs 0-3 with `--disaggregation-mode prefill`, `flashinfer_mxfp4` decode server on GPUs 4-7, NIXL/UCX KV transfer over RoCE, `sglang_router --pd-disaggregation`): coherent smoke answers and GSM8K-200 = 0.990 (`run_eval`) in two separate runs. (In the second run one request hit the 300 s disaggregation bootstrap timeout before its prefill started.) PD throughput was not measured.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup; `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 4096` (4096 prefill tokens per rank), `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, decode CUDA graphs on (prefill CUDA graphs are disabled for DeepSeek-V4 by SGLang's own rule), `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids`. Prefill: a dedicated rerun on 2026-10-15 with radix cache disabled, three rounds per point, all three backends on the same production tree. Decode: the earlier c7 session on the same production tree, one round per point; GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) in that session: 96.5 % / 97.0 % / 97.0 %.

**Prefill** (OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 64`, `--disable-radix-cache`), input tokens/s (TTFT mean / median / P99, ms). Both baselines run W4A8 (MXFP4 weights x MXFP8 activations, FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE) with the tokens all-gathered over attention DP and reduce-scattered after the MoE; `--ep-size 4` places whole experts per rank like this PR:

| ISL | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, EP4 | flashinfer_megamoe | vs TP / vs EP4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 12125 (2669 / 2630 / 3670) | 13853 (2334 / 2279 / 3243) | 24174 (1336 / 1291 / 1982) | 1.99x / 1.75x |
| 1024 | 12332 (5126 / 5289 / 6301) | 14165 (4462 / 4603 / 5483) | 25106 (2518 / 2583 / 3121) | 2.04x / 1.77x |
| 2048 | 12101 (9861 / 10774 / 11961) | 13854 (8611 / 9411 / 10469) | 24085 (4950 / 5367 / 6086) | 1.99x / 1.74x |
| 4096 | 11935 (17502 / 21537 / 23239) | 13644 (15287 / 18821 / 20285) | 23400 (8923 / 10887 / 11918) | 1.96x / 1.72x |

In this serving configuration, EP4 improves the baseline by about 1.14-1.15x and the MegaMoE backend is 1.72-1.77x faster than that EP4 baseline (1.96-2.04x over TP MoE). This comparison measures the complete backend, including communication and integration; it does not isolate kernel fusion alone.

Each prefill round has 524288 requested input tokens (`num-prompts = 524288 / ISL`), request rate infinity, concurrency 64, temperature 0, and client seeds 101, 102 and 103; a separate cold run is excluded. The server uses `--disable-radix-cache` and each benchmark passes `--flush-cache`. All 36 measured runs completed every request without errors; all output lengths are one token. The table reports medians of three run-level metrics (including run-level P99s), not pooled request percentiles. The largest per-point throughput range `(max-min)/median` across the three rounds was 0.8% / 0.6% / 3.1% for TP / EP4 / MegaMoE respectively. The runs were sequential on one host, so these are synthetic serving measurements, not a PD throughput or kernel microbenchmark result.

Decode uses seed 42, concurrency 4/16/64/256 and 32/32/128/512 requests respectively; all measured output lengths are 1024 tokens. These earlier decode runs retained radix caching and did not explicitly flush between cases.

**Decode** (ISL 128 / OSL 1024, ignore_eos), median TPOT (ms):

| concurrency (req/rank) | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, `--ep-size 4` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 (1) | 15.4 | 16.0 | 21.6 |
| 16 (4) | 21.0 | 22.0 | 27.1 |
| 64 (16) | 33.4 | 33.4 | 37.0 |
| 256 (64) | 61.7 | 60.9 | 60.2 |

Hence the prefill positioning. Decode CUDA graphs capture one bucket per batch size: with `--disable-cuda-graph` the median TPOT of this PR is 65.1 / 62.6 / 62.9 ms at concurrency 4 / 16 / 64 (mxfp4: 66.3 / 65.4 / 66.6 ms).

**Topology (supplementary, historical cache-enabled runs).** The kernel picks a per-peer transport: NCCL LSA (CUDA peer access over PCIe/NVLink) where peers can reach each other and NCCL GIN (GPU-initiated RDMA over the NIC) elsewhere. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` selects the table. Prefill, OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 128`, input tokens/s for ISL 2048 / 4096:

| cake layout | GPUs | flashinfer_mxfp4 (TP MoE, EP=1) | this PR, `lsa_where_reachable` (default) | this PR, `all_gin` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 / attn-DP4 / EP4 | 0-3, one CPU socket | 12126 / 12130 | 24283 / 23629 (2.00x / 1.95x) | 24563 / 23967 (2.03x / 1.98x) |
| TP8 / attn-DP8 / EP8 | 0-7, two CPU sockets | 13578 / 14855 | 40690 / 42221 (3.00x / 2.84x) | 41629 / 44673 (3.07x / 3.01x) |

At EP8 the two sockets have no CUDA peer path between them, so the default table runs LSA for the 24 directed off-diagonal peer pairs inside the sockets and GIN for the 32 directed pairs across sockets (56 off-diagonal pairs in total); an all-LSA table is not possible on this host. At EP8 this PR needed `--mem-fraction-static 0.70` on these 72 GB GPUs (at 0.80 the first MegaMoE launch ran out of memory); the EP8 rows of both backends use 0.70. GSM8K-200 (`run_eval`) was 0.985-0.990 in every layout.

## Motivation This PR adds an SGLang-native CUTLASS **MXFP4A8 fused MoE backend for SM90/Hopper**, targeting MXFP4-expert models such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The implementation keeps expert weights in MXFP4 (E2M1 with block-32 E8M0 scales), dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 E4M3, and executes both expert GEMMs on Hopper FP8 tensor cores. The current scope is deliberately limited to **TP deployments with EP=1**. `EP>1` is not supported by this PR and is rejected explicitly during weight initialization. ## Summary - Add an MXFP4-to-FP8 mixed-input CUTLASS path for SM90. - Add load-time Humming-compatible MXFP4 weight preprocessing. - Add an EP1 fused runtime covering routing metadata preparation, input permutation and quantization, GEMM1, SwiGLU, requantization, GEMM2, output permutation, router weighting, and top-k reduction. - Add shape-specialized SM90 schedulers for serving-time token buckets. - Preserve the existing INT4A8 path unchanged. - Add numerical tests for MXFP4 conversion, scale layouts, grouped GEMM, and cross-backend consistency against FlashInfer. The backend is selected with: ```bash --moe-runner-backend cutlass ``` ### Execution flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant X as BF16 input participant R as Top-k routing participant S as SGLang fused path participant F as FlashInfer participant W as MXFP4 weights participant Y as MoE output X->>R: tokens and topk=6 W-->>S: Humming-compatible view W-->>F: Humming view par SGLang EP1 path R->>S: GPU-built routing metadata S->>S: reorder + per-token FP8 quant S->>S: grouped GEMM1 S->>S: SwiGLU + FP8 requant S->>S: grouped GEMM2 S-->>Y: reorder + router-weight reduction and FlashInfer R->>F: topk IDs + router weights F->>F: bucketed tactic lookup F->>F: fused MoE body F-->>Y: fused finalize end Note over S,F: Same logical MXFP4 weights and routing inputs
Different runtime orchestration and scheduling ``` ## Implementation ### MXFP4A8 tensor-core path Weights remain in checkpoint-native MXFP4. Activations are quantized per token to FP8 E4M3. The E2M1 values `{0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6}` are exactly representable in E4M3, so the E2M1-to-E4M3 conversion uses a lossless signed-nibble lookup. The mixed-input mainloop derives the scale group from `TileK / PackedScalesNum`, allowing the existing INT4A8 group-128 path and the new MXFP4A8 group-32 path to share the same mainloop without changing INT4 behavior. ### Load-time weight preprocessing The EP1 path prepares one runtime representation after checkpoint loading: - interleaved MXFP4 weights; - folded E8M0 offsets; - one residual scale per expert. The representation follows the SM90 Humming preprocessing semantics. Runtime execution is implemented by SGLang AOT kernels. Only the fused representation is retained for EP1 to avoid storing two complete weight layouts on H20. ### Fused EP1 execution `cutlass_mxfp4a8_fused_moe_core` performs: 1. expert-offset, problem-size, and permutation preparation; 2. routed-input reorder and per-token FP8 quantization; 3. grouped GEMM1; 4. fused SwiGLU, optional clamp, and FP8 requantization; 5. grouped GEMM2; 6. output reorder, FP32 router-weight multiplication, `routed_scaling_factor`, and top-k reduction. For `M <= 64`, metadata preparation and shuffled input quantization use a bounded fused CUDA path. Larger batches use the AOT metadata and quantization kernels without host synchronization. Intermediate tensors are retained in reusable workspaces. ### SM90 scheduling The implementation includes: - a persistent single-warpgroup ping-pong kernel for tiny and arbitrary serving-time shapes; - a precomputed grouped scheduler with prebuilt TMA descriptors for validated large-M buckets; - a packed warp-shuffle GEMM2 epilogue. | Tokens | GEMM1 config | GEMM2 config | |---:|---:|---:| | `M <= 64` | 100 | 100 | | `M = 2048` | 313 | 313 | | `M = 4096` | 320 | 334 | | `M >= 8192` | 322 | 334 | | Other shapes | 101 | 101 | ## Validation ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash end-to-end A/B Hardware and runtime: - 8x NVIDIA H20; - native DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint; - TP8 / EP1; - FP8 KV cache and DSV4 attention; - separate fresh containers for the two backends; - identical package versions except for the locally built `sglang-kernel` wheel; - FlashInfer 0.6.18 W4A8 as the upstream baseline. Serving workload: - exact paired token-ID prompts; - 128 requests; - concurrency 32; - output length 1536; - repeat 1. | Input -> output | CUTLASS output tok/s | FlashInfer output tok/s | Throughput | Mean TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8192 -> 1536 | 1399.19 | 1247.18 | **+12.19%** | **-17.26%** | | 16384 -> 1536 | 933.52 | 814.49 | **+14.61%** | **-16.95%** | | 32768 -> 1536 | 541.48 | 466.34 | **+16.11%** | **-16.18%** | All 384 requests completed successfully. Neither server log contained a CUDA error, OOM, or traceback. ### GSM8K The complete 1319-question GSM8K set was evaluated with five fixed shots, temperature 0, 32 threads, and repeat 1. | Backend | Correct | Accuracy | |---|---:|---:| | CUTLASS MXFP4A8 | 1252 / 1319 | 94.9204% | | FlashInfer | 1246 / 1319 | 94.4655% | The paired discordance was 16 CUTLASS-only correct versus 10 Humming-only correct (exact McNemar `p=0.3269`). This run does not establish a statistically significant accuracy difference. ### Kernel and operator tests | Test suite | Result | |---|---:| | CUTLASS MXFP4 grouped GEMM | 11 passed | | CUTLASS vs FlashInfer fused MoE | 3 passed | | Existing INT4 grouped GEMM | 605 passed | | Focused DSV4 norm/RoPE | 16 passed | The cross-backend test generates one logical MXFP4 weight set and uses the same BF16 input, top-k IDs, and router weights for both implementations. It covers `M=1`, `M=16`, and `M=65` with DeepSeek-V4-Flash `topk=6`, and requires: - normalized L2 error `< 2.5%`; - cosine similarity `> 0.9995`. ## Limitations - Supported hardware: SM90/Hopper. - Supported expert-parallel configuration: **EP=1 only**. - `EP>1` is explicitly rejected; this PR does not claim a legacy or DeepEP fallback. - Hidden size must be divisible by 128; intermediate size must be divisible by 32 and may be padded for validated GEMM shapes. - The load-time representation reuses FlashInfer's SM90 preprocessing semantics; runtime execution uses SGLang AOT kernels. - The reported performance results are specific to DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 8x H20 with the configuration above. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Validate MXFP4, INT4, and DSV4 regressions. - [x] Provide complete GSM8K accuracy results. - [x] Provide paired end-to-end performance results against current upstream FlashInfer. - [ ] Add user-facing documentation if maintainers request it. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39389973536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973536) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39389973468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973468) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39389973442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973442)

## Motivation

On NPU, FP4-expert models routed through Fp8MoEMethod ( is_fp4_expert=True , e.g. MiMo-V2.5-Pro with modelopt_fp4) delegate execution to NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod kernels via the ASCEND MoE runner. However, process_weights_after_loading only runs Fp8MoEMethod 's own body, so the DeepEP dispatcher quant config was never set — dispatch fell back to BF16 and a separate DynamicMxQuant kernel ran before every grouped matmul (~15ms/layer at 16K-token prefill).

The native FP4 path ( NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , DSV4) already sets the same dispatcher config; the Fp8MoEMethod path was simply missing it.

## Modifications

- Declare the dispatch wire format as a DISPATCHER_QUANT_CONFIG class attribute on NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod ( low_latency=mxfp8 ; normal stays BF16 since A5 MXFP8 normal dispatch is intranode-only). The kernel that consumes the activations now owns the declaration, instead of each caller hand-writing platform-specific if/else patches.
- In Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading , pick the config up from the attached layer.w13_kernel when it declares one; otherwise keep the original checkpoint-dtype config. No _is_npu / is_fp4_expert branching — the attached kernel already encodes both.
- Reuse the same declaration in NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , replacing its hand-written copy.

## Motivation

MiMo-V2.5-Pro defines a per-model `attention_value_scale` that the attention forward applies to V before writing the KV cache and before the attention output (`v = v * v_scale`). On NPU this materializes as an extra `aclnnMuls` kernel per layer in every decode/verify step — ~2 ms/layer on MiMo-V2.5-Pro EP6 profiling (~8% of the attention section).

Attention is linear in V:

    softmax(qk) @ (s · V) ≡ s · (softmax(qk) @ V)

so multiplying the layer's `o_proj.weight` by `s` at load time reproduces the runtime `v * v_scale` exactly, and the per-token kernel disappears.

## Modifications

- Add `MiMoV2ForCausalLM._fold_attention_value_scale_into_o_proj`, called at the end of `load_weights`: for each attention layer with a `v_scale`, multiply `o_proj.weight.data` by `attention_value_scale` (when the config defines one) and clear `attn.v_scale` so the runtime multiply is skipped.
- Only floating-point o_proj weights are folded (MiMo FP4 checkpoints keep o_proj in bf16, so this covers the shipped configurations); a quantized o_proj keeps the runtime multiply and logs a warning.
- The KV cache now stores unscaled V. This stays self-consistent because every consumer of V (decode, target-verify, DFlash draft KV materialization) goes through the same layer's (folded) o_proj.
- MTP draft (`mimo_v2_nextn.py`) and DFlash draft (`dflash.py`) have independent weight loading and their own v_scale handling; they are unaffected.

## Motivation

On ROCm, Quark-quantized Kimi-K3 (`Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) stores attention weights as per-channel FP8. Two of those layers miss the FP8 kernels at decode:
- The KDA input projection runs as three separate linears (`[q,k,v,g]`, `f_a`, `b`).
- The MLA absorb dequantizes `kv_b` to BF16 and runs BF16 BMMs.

## Modifications

**`5e57539a9c` run the Quark per-channel FP8 KDA in-proj and MLA absorb on FP8 kernels on ROCm**
- Merge the Quark per-channel FP8 [q,k,v,g | f_a | b] KDA in-projection into one FP8 linear for decode.
- Pad the merged output to a multiple of 64 so it keeps AITER's preshuffled FP8 GEMM.
- Serve the Quark FP8 f_b from a BF16 copy so it uses the tiny GEMM and the fused KDA decode.
- Take the single in-proj GEMM path whenever the merged layer exists, not only when _bfa_w is set.
- Requantize the Quark per-channel FP8 kv_b to per-tensor FP8 so the MLA absorb BMMs run AITER a8w8.
- Gate the absorb requantization behind SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_MLA_ABSORB_FP8, on by default.
- Register SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND and keep SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND as a deprecated alias.

items.body:
# [Feat] [Intel] HiCache: Enable L1<->L2 support on XPU

## Motivation

HiCache, SGLang's hierarchical KV cache, is currently gated to CUDA and ROCm. This PR enables the **L1 (device) <-> L2 (host)** tier on Intel XPU: the host KV pools and the `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio` transfer kernels, which XPU gets from the out-of-tree `sgl-kernel-xpu` wheel.

**Scope: L2 only.** Nothing in this PR calls a storage backend, so it adds no NIXL dependency to the XPU image or CI. L3 (storage) on XPU is a separate, experimental follow-up.

**Only XPU code paths change.** CUDA, ROCm, NPU and CPU keep their upstream code. Every new runtime branch is under `_is_xpu`, and the 6 upstream lines this PR touches each keep their original behavior and gain an XPU alternative.

## Modifications

### 1. Keep XPU index tensors alive across L2 copies

- `L2TransferEngine._record_stream` recorded index tensors on the transfer stream only when `indices.is_cuda`, which is `False` on XPU. The caching allocator could then reuse an index tensor while an asynchronous copy was still reading it.
- The check is now `indices.is_cuda or indices.device.type == "xpu"`. CUDA/ROCm take the same branch as before, and other devices are unchanged.

### 2. Bind the XPU `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio` ops

New `mem_cache/pool_host/_kvcacheio.py` binds the 13 kvcacheio transfer ops on XPU, where they come from the out-of-tree `sgl-kernel-xpu` wheel.

- **CUDA/ROCm are untouched.** Each pool module keeps its `if _is_cuda or _is_hip: from sgl_kernel.kvcacheio import (...)` block and adds `elif _is_xpu:` importing the same names from the gate. In `mla.py` and `memory_pool_host.py` the old condition `_is_cuda or _is_hip or _is_xpu` becomes `_is_cuda or _is_hip`, with the same import list.
- **Each op is bound on its own via `getattr`.** The op set varies by `sgl-kernel-xpu` wheel, so a wheel missing `transfer_kv_all_layer_mla` stubs only that op and records it in `missing_ops`.
- **Off XPU the gate binds nothing.** Importing it only defines its helpers and the shared `MLA_KVCACHEIO_OPS` table; `missing_ops` stays empty.

| XPU build | result |
|---|---|
| all 13 ops present | all bound |
| some ops missing | the missing ops are stubbed; a pool whose `(io_backend, layout)` needs one is refused at construction |
| `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio` absent | every op stubbed; every host pool refused at construction |

### 3. Refuse unsupported host pools at construction (XPU)

- On XPU, `require_kvcacheio_ops(pool=..., layout=..., ops=...)` fails when a host pool is built, instead of mid-request in a cache-controller thread.
- **Every call is under `if _is_xpu:`**, so CUDA, ROCm, NPU and CPU never reach it. It is imported at module level, so a process that sees both CUDA and XPU (CUDA imports win) cannot hit a `NameError`.
- **Each pool declares a `_kvcacheio_ops = {io_backend: {layout: op names}}` table next to its transfer methods, defined only under `if _is_xpu:`.** Off XPU the attribute does not exist. The MLA, DSA indexer and both DeepSeek-V4 pools dispatch to the same ops and share the read-only `MLA_KVCACHEIO_OPS`.
- A pool is refused only when an op for **its own** `(io_backend, layout)` is missing. Pools with the check:
  - `MHATokenToKVPoolHost` (the Asymmetric, MXFP8 and HiSparse subclasses inherit it)
  - `MHATokenToKOnlyPoolHost`
  - `MLATokenToKVPoolHost`
  - `DSAIndexerPoolHost`
  - `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool` and `DeepSeekV4StateHostPool`
- **Server args are read lazily.** The check reads `get_memory().hicache_io_backend` only when some op is missing, so a complete wheel never needs published server args.
- **`is_dummy` MLA/DSA pools skip the check.** They are allocator metadata only and never reach a transfer op.
- **DeepSeek-V4:** `transfer_cache_dsv4_mla` is not a kvcacheio op. If the XPU wheel lacks it, the import becomes a stub instead of breaking the scheduler, and `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool` refuses at construction unless `page_aligned_only`.
- **Mamba is refused on XPU.** Its `transfer_kv_mamba_*` kernels are JIT-built from CUDA source here. The error names both `--enable-hierarchical-cache` and `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup=host_pool`.

### 4. Fail on a null pinned allocation (XPU)

- torch 2.13.0+xpu returns `data_ptr() == 0` from a failed pinned allocation instead of raising. Measured: 8 GiB succeeds, 2048 GiB returns null.
- This is pinned host memory for the L2 pool, sized from host RAM; it is unrelated to device free memory.
- `ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS["xpu"]` now points to `alloc_with_pin_memory_xpu`, which raises on a null buffer. Without it the pool is built on a null buffer and the first transfer faults in a cache-controller thread.
- An empty tensor also has `data_ptr() == 0`, so it is allowed. `alloc_with_pin_memory`, used by NPU and MUSA, and the CUDA `cudaHostRegister` default are unchanged.

### 5. CI

No workflow changes. The new XPU tests register in the existing per-commit suites (`stage-a-test-1-gpu-xpu`, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu`), and `pr-test-xpu.yml` already runs XPU CI for any changed test file with a per-commit `register_xpu_ci` (`scripts/ci/xpu/detect_xpu_test_changes.py`).

## Accuracy Tests

### XPU transfer round trip (`stage-a-test-1-gpu-xpu`)

`xpu/test_hicache_transfer_round_trip_xpu.py` checks that `backup_from_device_all_layer` -> `load_to_device_per_layer` is a **bit-exact identity**. It covers every `(io_backend, mem_layout)` pair the XPU build dispatches to: 5 MHA pairs and 2 MLA pairs, **13 distinct kernels** in total. Host indices are offset by one page from device indices, so a kernel that ignores either index tensor fails the round trip.


### XPU end-to-end (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu`, per commit)

- **`e2e/hicache/test_hicache_xpu_no_storage.py`:** L1+L2 on both io backends with `Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`.
- **`e2e/hicache/test_hicache_xpu_mla_kernels.py`:** one server per `(io_backend, mem_layout)`. The model is a locally generated 2-layer DeepseekV3 with real MLA dimensions, built once per file, so no private HF repo is needed.
- **Shared helper:** `python/sglang/test/hicache_xpu_common.py`.

What every restore case checks:

- **Restores are real.** Each restore asserts that `sglang:load_back_tokens_total` increases, so a pass means the KV actually crossed host -> device and was not served from the device radix cache.
- **Output is bit-exact.** Restored output is compared against a golden that is primed from the device tier. Only the tier differs between golden and restore, not the prefill path.
- **One skip per file is expected.** The abstract `_*Server` base class raises `SkipTest`; each config is a concrete subclass.


### CPU (`base-a-test-cpu`)

- `unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_kvcacheio_gate.py` (new). It needs no XPU: it parses the pool sources with `ast` and reloads the gate with `is_xpu` patched against a fake `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio`, so it runs on every PR, including CUDA-only ones that could break XPU.
  - **Table/dispatch sync.** Each pool's `_kvcacheio_ops` must match the kvcacheio ops its methods call: every called op declared (or the check would miss it), every declared op called (or the check would refuse a pool that works). `MambaPoolHost` (refused on XPU) and `UnifiedPageEnvelopeHostPool` (CUDA/ROCm only) are excluded by name.
  - **XPU-only.** Every `require_kvcacheio_ops` call must sit under an `_is_xpu` branch, be imported at module level, and every table must be defined under `if _is_xpu:`.
  - **Gate behavior.**
    - a complete XPU wheel binds every op and never reads server args;
    - an XPU wheel missing one op refuses only the pools and layouts that dispatch to it (MHA builds on every layout; MLA is refused on `kernel`/`layer_first` only);
    - XPU without the module refuses every pool;
    - on CUDA, ROCm, NPU and CPU the gate binds nothing and never reads server args.
- `unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_host_register.py`: a null buffer from `alloc_with_pin_memory_xpu` raises and an empty tensor does not; only `"xpu"` maps to the null-checked allocator.
- `unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`: `TestL2TransferRecordStream`, with stub index tensors because CPU CI has no XPU. XPU and CUDA index tensors are recorded and another accelerator is not; the old `is_cuda` predicate and a generic `!= "cpu"` predicate each fail one case.
- `unit/mem_cache/test_mem_pool_host.py`: `MambaPoolHost` refuses XPU at construction.
- Every new check is mutation-tested: removing the fix it guards fails it.

### Test Results

CPU rows ran on this commit. The XPU rows were measured on one Intel Arc Pro B60 .

| Test | Where | Result | Time |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_host_register.py` | CPU | 17 passed | 6.7 s |
| `unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_kvcacheio_gate.py` | CPU | 9 passed | 5.4 s |
| `unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py` | CPU | 23 passed, 1 skipped | 7.1 s |
| `unit/mem_cache/test_mem_pool_host.py` | CPU | 25 passed | 6.9 s |
| `xpu/test_hicache_transfer_round_trip_xpu.py` | XPU | 7 passed | 9.3 s (30 s) |
| `e2e/hicache/test_hicache_xpu_no_storage.py` | XPU | 2 passed | 96 s (400 s) |
| `e2e/hicache/test_hicache_xpu_mla_kernels.py` | XPU | 2 passed | 101 s (120 s) |

## Performance Tests

### Environment

- Hardware: 4x Intel Arc Pro B60, `tp=4`
- `--page-size 16`, `--max-total-tokens 16384`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`
### 1. Shared-prefix workload

**Model:** `Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`

**Workload:**

- `generated-shared-prefix`
- 32 groups x 2 prompts
- 2,048-token system prompt, 128-token question, 64 output tokens
- Concurrency 8
- Shared working set: 65,536 tokens (~4x L1)
- `--hicache-ratio 2.0`

| Configuration | Duration | Req/s | Output tok/s | p50 TTFT | Mean TTFT | p50 TPOT | p50 E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 39.6s | 1.62 | 103.4 | 781.6ms | 1521.5ms | 47.9ms | 3710.9ms |
| L2 | 43.8s | 1.46 | 93.6 | 795.7ms | 1666.7ms | 53.0ms | 4166.9ms |

L2 alone is slightly slower here. The working set is ~4x L1, and `--hicache-ratio 2.0` gives L2 room for only half of it, so most prefix lookups still miss and the host transfers are not offset by the prefill they save.

This PR's goal for L2 is a correct tier: the transfer kernels and host pools, verified bit-exact. That tier is what the storage tier builds on, and the TTFT improvement from hierarchical cache on XPU will be reported in the L3 follow-up.

### 2. Low-prefix-reuse workload

**Model:** `Llama3.1-8B`

**Workload:** random ShareGPT prompts, 200 prompts, concurrency 32, `--hicache-ratio 3`.

| Configuration | Req/s | Output tok/s | Total tok/s | Median TTFT | p99 TTFT | Median TPOT | Median E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 2.16 | 452.9 | 1108.4 | 151ms | 7454ms | 53.3ms | 8294ms |
| L2 | 1.86 | 389.2 | 952.5 | 185ms | 8601ms | 61.9ms | 9826ms |

This workload has little cross-request prefix reuse, so the tiering and transfer overhead is not offset by cache hits. It is the complementary case to the shared-prefix benchmark: whether HiCache helps depends on how much prefix reuse the workload has.

### 3. AgentX trace replay

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct` |
| Hardware | Intel Arc Pro B60 (cards 4-7) |
| Tensor Parallelism | TP=4 |
| Host Memory | 1,003 GiB DRAM |
| NUMA Nodes | 2 |
| Context Length | 131,072 |
| Workload | AgentX trace replay |
| Requests | 129 total, 120 accepted |
| Max New Tokens | 2 |
| Concurrency Levels | 1, 4, 8, 12, 16 |

| Concurrency | HiCache Hit Rate | Baseline Hit Rate | HiCache Runtime | Baseline Runtime | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 91.9% | 90.3% | 159 s | 172 s | 1.08x |
| 4 | 89.9% | 86.1% | 181 s | 230 s | 1.27x |
| 8 | 90.0% | 83.8% | 179 s | 265 s | 1.48x |
| 12 | 89.6% | 85.1% | 180 s | 239 s | 1.33x |
| 16 | 89.5% | 79.4% | 189 s | 332 s | 1.76x |

This is the workload HiCache is built for: long agentic contexts with heavy prefix reuse. With HiCache the hit rate stays at about 90% at every concurrency level, while the baseline's falls from 90.3% to 79.4% as more concurrent requests evict each other's prefixes from the device cache. The runtime gap widens with it, from 1.08x at concurrency 1 to 1.76x at 16.

No performance change for CUDA/ROCm: their code paths are unchanged.

## Known gaps

- **Mamba on XPU is still refused.** `pool_host/mamba.py` refuses XPU at construction. Routing it to the `sgl-kernel-xpu` Mamba ops is a separate change with its own tests.
- **HiSparse imports one op directly.** On XPU, `hisparse_memory_pool.py` still imports `transfer_kv_all_layer_mla` from `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio`, so a wheel without that op or without the module fails at import rather than at pool construction. HiSparse is left unchanged in this PR.
- **NPU and MUSA still skip `record_stream` for index tensors.** `l2_transfer.py` checks `indices.is_cuda`, which is `False` there too. This PR adds only the XPU case.
- **`DSAIndexerPoolHost` can now be built on XPU when the wheel supplies the ops, but no DSA model has been run on XPU.**
- **The table/dispatch sync test compares op sets per pool, not per `(io_backend, layout)` branch.** A mis-assigned op fails at first transfer with a `RuntimeError` naming it, not at construction.


## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run` clean on all touched files
- [x] CUDA/ROCm/NPU/CPU code paths unchanged; every new branch is XPU-only
- [x] No new dependency for XPU CI (L2 needs no storage backend, so no NIXL)
- [x] CPU tests pass; every new check is mutation-tested
- [x] XPU transfer round trip: 7/7
- [x] `test_hicache_xpu_no_storage`: 2/2
- [x] `test_hicache_xpu_mla_kernels`: 2/2
- [x] L2 benchmarks on XPU

## Summary

Adapt GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsa) DSA prefill context parallelism to the CP V2 strategy flow, mirroring the DSV4 CP V2 support merged in #39427. After CP V1 was deprecated upstream, the NPU DSA path still referenced removed V1 metadata fields and could no longer run with --enable-prefill-cp.

## Changes

- **ascend_backend.py**: add prepare_dsa_cp_metadata which builds per-token local metadata for the Ascend sparse kernels (q/kv lengths from sharded local positions, per-token block-table rows selected by local batch ids); rewrite do_cp_balance_attn to a single npu_sparse_flash_attention call on the strategy-sharded local Q (no V1 prev/next balance split).
- **dsa_npu_indexer.py**: read V2 local metadata instead of the removed V1 attn_cp_metadata fields (actual_seq_q_prev_tensor / kv_len_prev_tensor / ...); rewrite do_npu_cp_balance_indexer as a single npu_lightning_indexer call.
- **deepseek_v2.py**: prepare DSA CP metadata at the inner-model entry (the eager CP runner invokes DeepseekV2Model directly); restore rebuild_cp_kv_cache, gathering the rank-local latent KV into full sequence order via cp_gather_full_sequence_states.
- **forward_mha.py**: on NPU with CP active, gather kv_a/k_pe to full sequence order before writing, since out_cache_loc spans the full sequence under CP V2.
- **unit tests**: add `test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py` covering the zigzag/interleave block layout, local row selection, padding alignment, the `is_cp_active` gate, and the GLM DSA layer-split helpers.

The first commit fixes the attn_cp_tp_broadcast_pyobj broadcast order for attn-CP > 1 (broadcast along the attn-TP 0 line first, then TP).

## Testing

Full-model verification on a 4-node Ascend 910B3 cluster (32 NPUs/node) with GLM-5.2-w8a8 (GlmMoeDsa) in PD disaggregation:

- **Prefill** (2 nodes, 209/212): `--tp-size 8 --pp-size 4 --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 --mem-fraction-static 0.88`, NEXTN spec (num-steps 1, draft 2)
- **Decode** (2 nodes, 216/217): `--tp-size 32 --dp-size 32 --ep-size 32`, NEXTN spec (num-steps 3, draft 4)
- Key envs: `DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2048`, `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=18,20,24,16`, `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ALL_CP_RANKS_TRANSFER=1`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1`, `MALLOC_CHECK_=3`
- Client: vllm bench serve through the sglang PD router (16 prompts, concurrency 4, input 65536 / output 2500)

### Throughput / latency results

| config | result | TTFT mean / median / P99 | TPOT | throughput |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| zigzag + chunk 4096 | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 9.45s / 5.85s / 26.05s | 26.89 ms | 3370 tok/s |
| interleave + chunk 8192 (fixed len) | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 9.12s / 6.08s / 20.05s | 25.70 ms | 3570 tok/s |
| interleave + chunk 8192 (variable input 40960–90112) | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 7.82s / 6.94s / 15.53s | 25.85 ms | 3550 tok/s |

The zigzag + chunk 8192 crash is a deep_ep CAM dispatch buffer overflow (`HCCL_BUFFSIZE is too SMALL`, 3304MB needed > 2048MB) triggered when a pass dispatches the whole 8076-token batch per rank; chunk 4096 caps the per-rank dispatch at ~1.78GB. Interleave keeps CP active on every pass (1024 tokens/rank, ~604MB), so it is safe with chunk 8192.

### Accuracy (gpqa_diamond)

evalscope 90.4%

### Unit tests

`test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py` — **21/21 passed** (CPU, no NPU needed):

```
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py -v
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# GLM-5.2-w8a8 2p2d (prefill-decode disaggregation) launcher.
# Same script on all 4 nodes; the role is picked from the local IP.
#   prefill (2p): 192.168.25.209, 192.168.25.212   tp8 x pp4 = 32 cards
#   decode  (2d): 192.168.25.216, 192.168.25.217   tp32 = 32 cards
# KV pool capacity: --mem-fraction-static 0.88 gives the decode pool ~82k
# tokens (>= 68036 needed for 64k in + 2.5k out).

echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor >/dev/null 2>&1
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 >/dev/null 2>&1
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0 >/dev/null 2>&1
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000 >/dev/null 2>&1

export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
unset https_proxy http_proxy HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

# ---- common env ----
export TRANSFORMERS_VERBOSITY=error

The two-call variant splits the local Q into prev/next halves and issues two `npu_sparse_flash_attention` calls with per-sequence metadata. End-to-end performance is identical (<0.5% difference), so this PR ships the single-call implementation for simplicity.

items.body:
## Motivation GLM-5.2/5.3 decode on MI355X spends a material part of each step in the MoE layer. The existing runner boundary receives already-materialized top-k IDs and weights, so a model-specific kernel cannot optimize across router projection, top-k, route sorting, expert scheduling, activation quantization, routed experts, and the shared expert. This PR adds an **explicit, strict, whole-layer Triton Gluon MoE backend** for the audited GLM Quark MXFP4 contract. Its main optimization is not a standalone faster top-k operation: the selected routes directly become the expert schedule, removing the generic `topk_ids -> moe_sorting -> expert GEMM` handoff. The backend is opt-in and fail-closed. `auto` never selects it, unsupported contracts raise before execution, and a requested Gluon path never silently falls back to AITER or another MoE runner. ## Modifications ### 1. What this adds - `gluon` as a `MoeRunnerBackend` choice. - A reusable whole-layer `GluonMoeBackend` interface with model-specific binding, eager weight preparation, execution, and output ABI validation. - A GLM-5.2/5.3 implementation for serialized Quark W4A4 MXFP4 target experts and the audited BF16 NextN expert layout on gfx950. - Shape-family kernels for decode, speculative verification, and prefill, including continuous TP4/EP1 and TP8/EP1 coverage through a 32K prefill chunk. - TP/EP-aware shared-expert handling and reuse of SGLang's existing post-expert collective/finalization path. Enable the target and speculative paths explicitly: ```bash --moe-runner-backend gluon \ --speculative-moe-runner-backend gluon ``` ### 2. Kernel design The optimized layer owns this model-specific sequence: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph A["Current SGLang + AITER boundary"] A0["BF16 hidden states"] --> A1["router GEMM"] A1 --> A2["M x 256 logits"] A2 --> A3["biased sigmoid top-8"] A3 --> A4["dense IDs + weights"] A4 --> A5["generic moe_sorting
count, bucket, pad, publish metadata"] A5 --> A6["quantize + GEMM1 + activation + GEMM2"] A6 --> A7["shared expert + add"] end subgraph G["GLM Triton Gluon whole-layer path"] G0["BF16 hidden states"] --> G1["router projection + input quant work
co-scheduled in one launch grid"] G1 --> G2["fixed 256-expert sigmoid top-8"] G2 --> G3{"active-token family"} G3 -->|"tiny M"| G4["selection/expert CTAs share a launch;
expert CTAs recompute the needed route rank"] G3 -->|"medium M"| G5["selection directly emits expert tickets,
sorted routes, and job descriptors"] G3 -->|"large M"| G6["chunk histogram + prefix/scatter
and bucketed grouped projections"] G4 --> G7["MXFP4 experts + shared expert"] G5 --> G7 G6 --> G7 end ``` Important details: - **Tiny M:** the router uses split-K CDNA4 MFMA work to expose enough CTAs on MI355X. Selection is compile-time specialized for 256 experts/top-8. The up-projection launch consumes the selected route directly instead of waiting for a generic sort. - **Medium M:** top-k appends routes directly to expert buckets and publishes the descriptors consumed by the expert projection. - **Large M:** chunked counting, prefix/scatter, and bucketed projections cover prefill shapes. The 32K family splits large routed-partial/code buffers so every gfx950 buffer address remains below the 4-GiB window. - **Quantization:** router projection and activation quantization are independent CTAs in the same launch grid; this removes a host launch and lets both work classes occupy the device together. They are not incorrectly described as a single CTA reading the input once. - **Shared expert:** TP/EP1 target execution consumes SGLang's normal appended shared-expert representation (257 experts). EP and NextN keep the native shared expert and add it before SGLang's existing collective. The isolated measurements below show that standalone top-k is approximately tied with AITER. The useful difference is the producer/consumer boundary: ```text AITER: router -> top-k metadata -> generic MoE sort -> expert work Gluon: router/quant -> top-k becomes the expert schedule -> expert work ``` ### rocprofiler-sdk kernel decomposition To separate GPU work from Python/dispatcher/launch overhead, the full TP8/EP1 MoE call was profiled at PR HEAD `317b7156d` with rocprofiler-sdk 1.1.0 (`--kernel-trace --marker-trace --stats`). Each AITER and Gluon arm was enclosed in its own ROCTx range and repeated 100 times on MI355X. `GPU active` below is the sum of device kernel durations per call. `GPU span` is from the first kernel start to the final kernel end under tracing; its parenthesized component is time between kernels and is profiler-sensitive. The `full MoE` column retains the low-overhead HIP-event result from the table above rather than treating traced wall time as application latency. | M | Path | Kernels / layer | GPU active | Traced GPU span (inter-kernel gaps) | Full MoE, low-overhead | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | AITER | 15 | 60.82 us | 649.17 us (587.41 us) | 574.97 us | | 1 | Gluon | 4 | 13.47 us | 70.76 us (57.44 us) | 99.42 us | | 16 | AITER | 14 | 95.57 us | 611.47 us (516.93 us) | 543.89 us | | 16 | Gluon | 3 | 39.05 us | 63.12 us (24.06 us) | 94.34 us | | 32 | AITER | 15 | 119.22 us | 657.49 us (537.73 us) | 706.99 us | | 32 | Gluon | 5 | 64.30 us | 104.74 us (40.52 us) | 159.48 us | The exact AITER device-time decomposition is: | AITER stage | M=1 | M=16 | M=32 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Router matmul, including BF16-to-FP32 cast where present | 2.69 us | 6.39 us | 7.78 us | | Biased grouped top-k | 4.06 us | 4.96 us | 4.89 us | | Generic route metadata sort/pad | 6.25 us | 9.72 us | 14.06 us | | Routed input quantization + scatter | 2.76 us | 4.25 us | 4.68 us | | Routed gate/up GEMM + SiLU/multiply | 18.11 us | 27.87 us | 36.77 us | | Routed activation quantization + scatter | 2.67 us | 3.02 us | 3.81 us | | Routed down GEMM | 3.82 us | 14.42 us | 19.68 us | | Shared input quantization | 2.15 us | 2.88 us | 3.34 us | | Shared gate/up GEMM, including split-K reduce | 7.90 us | 6.26 us | 7.04 us | | Shared SiLU + multiply | 3.75 us | 8.15 us | 9.15 us | | Shared activation quantization | 1.51 us | 1.96 us | 2.18 us | | Shared down GEMM | 3.43 us | 3.40 us | 3.47 us | | Routed + shared final add | 1.73 us | 2.27 us | 2.37 us | | **Total GPU active** | **60.82 us** | **95.57 us** | **119.22 us** | Gluon performs the same logical work with fused shape-specific stages: | Gluon kernel/stage | M=1 | M=16 | M=32 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Router GEMM + routed/shared input quantization | 2.48 us | 3.25 us | 3.60 us | | Top-k scheduling + routed/shared gate/up GEMM | 5.18 us | - | - | | Top-k scheduling + routed/shared gate/up + activation quantization | - | 23.91 us | - | | Top-k to expert-job schedule | - | - | 4.61 us | | Routed/shared gate/up GEMM + activation quantization | - | - | 33.80 us | | Activation + quantization | 2.52 us | - | - | | Routed/shared down GEMM + weighted reduction | 3.30 us | 11.89 us | - | | Routed/shared down GEMM | - | - | 18.10 us | | Weighted route reduction + shared add | - | - | 4.19 us | | **Total GPU active** | **13.47 us** | **39.05 us** | **64.30 us** | This changes the interpretation of the earlier isolated timings. At `M=1`, the Gluon `_router_linear` device body is **not** slower: it takes `2.48 us` while also quantizing routed and shared inputs, versus `2.69 us` for AITER's router-only GEMM. The earlier `17-18 us` versus `8-9 us` result measured the complete launch boundary, so it exposed launcher/dispatcher latency rather than slower router arithmetic. The current small-M optimization target should therefore not be the `2.48 us` router body in isolation. ### 3. SGLang integration, isolation, and support matrix The integration sits above `MoeRunnerCore`, because that interface starts after routing has already been computed. The runtime flow is: ```text explicit Gluon selection -> validate quant/model/runtime contract -> bind GLM backend -> prepare packed weights after checkpoint load and before CUDA graph capture -> dispatch by TP/EP, target/NextN, and active M -> validate rank-local output tensor ABI -> existing SGLang _finalize_normal_output / post_experts_all_reduce ``` Isolation from other paths: - `auto` never selects Gluon; AITER, Triton, FlashInfer, MegaMoE, DeepEP, CPU, and other models retain their existing behavior. - GLM modules and Gluon kernels are imported lazily only after explicit selection. - Binding validates `model_type`, hidden/intermediate dimensions, 256 routed experts, sigmoid normalized top-8, quant ABI, gfx950, TP/EP-local shapes, shared-expert state, stream mode, A2A, EPLB, MoE DP, and routed scaling. - Quark layout preparation is owned by the selected backend; Gluon does not construct a dummy AITER runner. - Unsupported M/topology/model/quant combinations raise an actionable error. There is no native/AITER fallback from the Gluon backend. Current audited matrix: | Total TP | EP | Rank-local routed experts | Rank-local intermediate | Target/NextN M coverage | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 1 | 256 | 512 | 1..32768 | | 4 | 4 | 64 | 2048 | 1..16768 | | 8 | 1 | 256 | 256 | 1..32768 | | 8 | 2 | 128 | 512 | 1..16768 | | 8 | 4 | 64 | 1024 | 1..16768 | | 8 | 8 | 32 | 2048 | 1..16768 | Current model scope: - GLM-5.2/5.3 `glm_moe_dsa` target with serialized Quark W4A4 MXFP4 experts. - GLM NextN/EAGLE draft with the exact audited BF16 expert ABI. This is intentionally not a generic Gluon MoE claim. Future fixed-topology MoEs can reuse the backend boundary, but each model still needs its own strict validator, weight-layout adapter, routing semantics, kernel family, correctness comparison, and performance evidence. The most direct next extension is another GLM-family Quark MXFP4 shape; unrelated models should not be enabled by relaxing the current checks. ## Accuracy Tests ### 4. Kernel correctness - Low-M old/new Gluon schedule comparison at M=1..8: exact bitwise match. - Router/top-k isolation at M=1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128: - identical dense logits: top-8 ID match fraction `1.0`; - maximum top-k weight difference `<= 5.96e-8`; - production split-logit selector vs. dense selector: IDs match `1.0`, weights exactly equal. - EP2/EP4/EP8 compact kernels vs. rank-masked AITER at M=65,96,192,255: - all outputs finite; - relative L2 ranges: `0.004556-0.004568` (EP2), `0.004146-0.004172` (EP4), `0.003849-0.003886` (EP8); - maximum absolute error `<= 9.77e-4`. - Large-M TP8/EP1 Gluon vs. AITER at M=128..32768: relative L2 `1.81%-2.33%`, consistent with different MXFP4 quantization/accumulation order. ### 5. End-to-end correctness Current integration was exercised on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 with EAGLE/NextN, FP8 KV cache, DSA Triton attention, and CUDA graphs: | Topology / arm | Result | |---|---| | TP4/EP4, AITER vs. Gluon | 8/8 exact response texts and 8/8 exact output-token ID sequences | | TP4/EP1, AITER vs. Gluon default shared fusion | 8/8 exact texts and token IDs | | TP4/EP1, AITER vs. Gluon with `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` | 8/8 exact texts and token IDs | Logs confirm the intended shared policy on every rank (EP target/NextN native; EP1 target fused and NextN native) and contain no fallback, skipped Gluon dispatch, assertion, runtime exception, memory access fault, or GPU fault. Strict AgentX functional canaries using the InferenceX workload configuration also completed for TP8/EP2, EP4, and EP8 with target and draft Gluon enabled: 16 backend reports per topology, zero skipped dispatches, zero request/benchmark errors, and no fallback. ### 6. GSM8K **Score: `0.9437` (94.37%, 1,240/1,314 correct).** The full run completed without request errors in 896.44 s at 146.98 output tok/s. This is above the existing 0.92 MI35x GSM8K accuracy threshold used by SGLang's GLM MXFP4 accuracy coverage. Configuration: - full 1,314-question GSM8K test set, 5-shot completion prompt; - GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4/EP1, target + NextN Gluon; - EAGLE `3/4/1`, FP8 KV cache, Triton DSA, CUDA graph; - `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`, 256 client threads, temperature 0, maximum 512 output tokens; - strict backend: no fallback. This run also covers the TP4/EP1 large-prefill family. An initial run exposed a real coverage boundary at `M=16802`; the implementation was extended to the full 32K chunk instead of reducing the prefill chunk or hiding the shape behind a fallback. A separate strict request with exactly 32,768 prompt tokens then completed successfully (`prompt_tokens=32768`, one generated token, 8.49 s E2E) with no runtime/GPU error or fallback. ### 7. Test inventory Latest local validation on MI355X: - `72 passed` across: - `test/registered/unit/models/test_gluon_moe_backend.py` - `test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_construction_isolation.py` - `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_fused_shared_expert_scaling.py` - `test/registered/unit/models/test_glm_nextn_moe_ptpc.py` - Continuous dispatch tests enumerate every integer M in each supported range and assert strict rejection immediately outside the audited ranges. - Official Ruff error selection (`F401,F821,F823,UP037`): pass. - Ruff format check over all 25 changed Python files: pass. - `git diff --check`: pass. - Full repository CI: pending; this PR is intentionally opened as Draft. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Microbenchmark method - AMD Instinct MI355X, one rank of TP8/EP1 unless stated otherwise. - AITER `acf8fdf9307431ece8ee275971c41cb3d1a7020b`. - PyTorch `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4`, Triton `3.8.0`. - 20 warmups, 200 timed repetitions, alternating arm order, HIP-event medians. - The AITER baseline includes SGLang's real small-M sorting patch and native shared-expert work. - Measurements were collected on equivalent pre-rebase kernel revisions; the rebased integration and 32K TP4 adapter were subsequently correctness-tested as described above. #### Route preparation decomposition (microseconds) | M | AITER router + top-k + sort | Gluon router + quant + select/schedule | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 62.16 | 32.94 | 1.89x | | 8 | 62.86 | 31.96 | 1.97x | | 16 | 61.48 | 31.90 | 1.93x | | 32 | 200.78 | 47.40 | 4.24x | | 64 | 190.74 | 52.58 | 3.63x | | 128 | 175.76 | 47.06 | 3.73x | At M=1..16, AITER's standalone router is about 2x faster and standalone top-k is approximately tied. items.title: [Fix] glm47: Disable tool grammar for `tool_choice="none"`

labels.name: run-ci
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

items.body:
## Motivation

With `--tool-call-parser glm47`, a request that supplies tools but explicitly sets `tool_choice="none"` still receives the GLM47 `full_assistant_ebnf` grammar.

That grammar describes a complete assistant turn. Reaching its terminal state finishes generation through the grammar path, which does not consult `ignore_eos`. An `ignore_eos=true` request can therefore stop at the model's end-of-turn token instead of reaching `max_tokens`, even though the request disabled tool calls.

### Behavior scope

| Request | Expected behavior | Ownership |
|---|---|---|
| No `tools` | Do not install the GLM47 tool-call grammar | Already fixed and tested by #39273 |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="none"` | Do not install the GLM47 tool-call grammar | Core fix in this PR |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="auto"` | Preserve the existing GLM47 grammar behavior | Regression coverage |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="required"` | Preserve the existing behavior | Regression coverage |
| `tools` + named tool choice | Preserve named-tool selection semantics | Regression coverage |
| Tools on `system`/`developer` messages | Include them in the active GLM47 grammar | Adjacent consistency fix requested during review |

### Relationship to #39273

The original version of this PR covered two cases:

1. requests with no tools; and
2. requests with tools plus `tool_choice="none"`.

While this PR was under review, #39273 independently added the `bool(effective_tools)` guard and a no-tools regression test as part of its GLM-5.3 work. Commit `f17f7705a5a67c137edf279edfdbd5460f2ceb6e` therefore already fixed case 1.

This branch was subsequently rebased onto main commit `4b384df0c94dbd0fe30627c27c98c0441b4ebd96`, which contains #39273. The duplicated no-tools production change and duplicated test were removed. The remaining core fix in this PR is case 2: tools are available, but the request explicitly disables tool calls with `tool_choice="none"`.

The no-tools history is retained here so reports that found the original analysis through this PR can follow that part of the fix to #39273.

## Modifications

Scope the GLM47 grammar to requests that provide tools and allow tool calls:

```python
glm_constraint = (
    self.tool_call_parser == "glm47"
    and bool(effective_tools)
    and request.tool_choice != "none"
    and not any(tool.function.strict for tool in effective_tools)
)
```

`auto`, `required`, and named-tool choices retain their existing grammar behavior. Other tool-call parsers are unchanged.

### Message-scoped tool consistency

`_effective_tools(request)` includes tools declared on `system` and `developer` messages. That effective set decides whether the GLM47 grammar is active, but the parser previously received only top-level `request.tools`. A request with message-scoped tools could therefore activate a grammar that omitted those functions.

The GLM47 parser now receives `effective_tools`. The regression test uses the real XGrammar parser and verifies message-scoped tools for `auto`, `required`, and named-tool choices, as well as the disabled `none` case.

### Test cleanup

- Keep the existing #39273 no-tools regression test.
- Remove the combined mocked no-tools/none test, which duplicated #39273 and the retained real-parser matrix.
- Remove the mocked auto test, which passed before this fix and only checked mock-result propagation.

Deliberately not changed:

- GLM47 grammar generation or grammar-terminal finish handling.
- Generic Jinja rendering of message-scoped tools, which affects multiple model families and needs separate cross-model coverage.
- Template compatibility for the `developer` role.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward code or kernel is changed. The checks below validate request semantics and grammar construction rather than model accuracy.

### Unit tests

Environment:

- Python 3.12.3
- pytest 9.1.1
- XGrammar available in the test image

Command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py \
  -k glm47 -v
```

On baseline `4b384df0c94dbd0fe30627c27c98c0441b4ebd96`, with the regression test applied but without the production fix:

```text
24 failed, 2 passed, 154 deselected, 16 warnings
```

The existing #39273 no-tools test passed. The new matrix failed for the message-scoped-tool cases and, importantly for this PR, for every `tool_choice="none"` subtest, including the case with a top-level tool.

With the fix applied:

```text
2 passed, 154 deselected, 16 warnings, 24 subtests passed
```

The complete serving-chat unit file was also run on the fixed snapshot:

```bash
