```bash
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py -v
```

```text
156 passed, 63 warnings, 126 subtests passed in 46.16s
```

### GLM-5.3 end-to-end reproduction

The E2E comparison specifically tested **tools plus `tool_choice="none"`**; it was not a no-tools test.

Source snapshots:

- Before: main commit `99463390f83a39776d452ba12199941b96a4f36f`
- After: the same source snapshot plus the production diff from local fix `c5649e50245567827c63ac9d9dc3fafb2334a00b`
- The relevant production code in that fix is identical to the subsequently rebased branch.

Hardware and model:

- 1 node with 8 x NVIDIA H200 GPUs
- Model path: `/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3`
- Served model name: `glm-5.3`
- Container tag: `sglang:dev-cu13-260921` 
- Launch requested TP=8 and DP-attention DP=8. The effective server log reported `tp_size=8`, `attn_dp_size=8`, and `dp_size=1`.
- The launch command passed `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`; the normalized server arguments logged an effective `chunked_prefill_size=4096`.
- `SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1` was set. 

Server command:

```bash

PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/zhipuai/GLM-5.3 \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --context-length 102400 \
  --tp 8 \

  --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \

  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \

```

Request, repeated five times against each server:

```bash

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  --data-binary @- <<'JSON'
{
  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Answer exactly with the word OK and nothing else."
    }
  ],
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "none",
  "temperature": 0,
  "seed": 42,
  "ignore_eos": true,
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "stop": null,
  "stream": false

```

Results:

| Snapshot | Completion tokens (5 runs) | Finish reason | `matched_stop` | Tool calls |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Baseline `99463390f8` | 66, 61, 47, 54, 67 | `stop` for all runs | 154827 for all runs | none |
| Fix `c5649e5024` | 300, 300, 300, 300, 300 | `length` for all runs | null for all runs | none |

Expected behavior: because the request explicitly disables tool calls and sets `ignore_eos=true`, no tool grammar should be installed and generation should continue until the 300-token cap. The fixed snapshot did so in all five runs.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark was run or claimed. Requests that continue to use the GLM47 grammar retain the same grammar-masking path. This PR only removes an inapplicable grammar from requests that explicitly disable tool calls.

items.title: [Fix] attention: Pad the TileLang sparse MLA prefill output back to the padded extend batch
items.body:
## Summary

**TL;DR: This PR extends #42896's output padding to the `[1, rows, heads, dim]` layout of the TileLang sparse MLA prefill kernel, so padded extend batches on that path run instead of crashing.** #42896, now on main, pads the attention output back to the padded batch only when rows are in the output's first dimension. The TileLang kernel's output therefore keeps only the real rows, and the next layer fails on the row count. This PR pads that layout as well. Other output layouts keep main's code path: the fa3 and triton attention backends give bit-identical outputs with and without this PR.

- **Enables:** GLM-5.3-Flash on its H200 cookbook pairing (BF16 KV + TileLang) now runs with an all-to-all MoE backend (MegaMoE) or with DP attention + MTP; on main both crash within 30 s of a gsm8k run. DeepSeek-V3.2 with DeepEP and TileLang prefill runs as well.
- **Accuracy:** on setups where main crashes, gsm8k now runs to the end: **91.9%** on GLM-5.3-Flash, in line with main's default `flashmla_sparse` prefill on that setup (91.8%); **91.7%** on GLM-5.3-Flash with DP attention + MTP; **95.8%** on DeepSeek-V3.2 with DeepEP.
- **Cost:** for this layout, one copy of the output into the padded output buffer, the same copy other backends' outputs already take. Only padded extend batches reach this code, and main crashes on them with this layout. No new flags or environment variables.

## Motivation

#42896 runs attention on the real rows of a padded extend batch and then pads the output back to the batch's rows. MLP sync can pad the batch when an all-to-all MoE backend (`--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` or `deepep`) runs at attention TP > 1, or under DP attention. The padding step in `_attention_on_real_rows` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/graph_utils.py`) expects rows in the output's first dimension. `tilelang_sparse_fwd` runs its kernel on `q.unsqueeze(0)` and returns `[1, rows, heads, dim]`, so the output is not padded and the next layer gets fewer rows than the batch:

- `ValueError: input tensor must be the same size as output size times world size` in the attention-TP reduce-scatter (GLM-5.3-Flash with MegaMoE);
- `ValueError: Mismatched mR.shape[0]` in the fused residual add-RMSNorm (GLM-5.3-Flash's MTP draft extend under DP attention, and DeepSeek-V3.2 with DeepEP).

v0.5.22, released on 2026-10-19, includes #42896 but not this fix.

It takes three things:
- `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang`;
- a padded extend batch on the sparse path: on H200, one whose longest sequence is over 2,048 tokens, in the target model or in the MTP draft model;
- a batch that runs outside a captured prefill CUDA graph: by default for MLA models, any batch over 2,048 tokens, or every batch with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`.

On ROCm, `--dsa-prefill-backend triton` (`triton_sparse_mla_fwd`) returns the same layout and takes the same new branch; we have not run it on ROCm.

GLM-5.3-Flash's H200 cookbook command uses BF16 KV with TileLang, so adding an all-to-all MoE backend, or DP attention with MTP, to it reaches this crash.

Repro (8x H200; on main every rank raises the first error above):
```bash
sglang serve --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --trust-remote-code --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \
  --disable-overlap-schedule --disable-shared-experts-fusion --max-running-requests 32 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --context-length 131072
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-shots 20 --num-examples 1319 --num-threads 32 \
  --max-tokens 512 --api completion
```

items.body:
## Summary

Fix Qwen3.5 dense serving on Ascend 950 across Gemma RMSNorm, multimodal rotary positions, and ModelSlim MXFP8 scale loading.

- Route ordinary `GemmaRMSNorm` and `Gemma3RMSNorm` through the stable `sgl_kernel_npu.norm.gemma_rmsnorm.npu_gemma_rms_norm` API. The wheel selects the provider at build time: native Gemma RMSNorm on Ascend 910B/910C, or standard RMSNorm with `1 + weight` on Ascend 950. Preserve the existing `torch_npu` fallback for older Ascend 910 wheels and document the required Ascend 950 package.
- Use `torch_npu.npu_add_rms_norm` with cached `gemma_weight` for the residual path at every hidden size. Reuse the same cached scales in the Qwen3.5 fused NPU prefill path, avoiding repeated `1 + weight` operations.
- Preserve three-axis multimodal positions in NPU prefill and route two-dimensional positions away from the ordinary NPU RoPE operator. Decode keeps its existing fused path.
- Round up ModelSlim MXFP8 scale placeholders, pad odd scale counts for the kernel pair layout, and align unaligned row-parallel shards to checkpoint quantization blocks. For example, `K=4304` requires 135 scales; TP ranks whose shard starts inside a block must share its scale and pad both weights and inputs to the same block boundary.

## Dependency

The ordinary Ascend 950 Gemma path requires a matching target wheel containing sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#638, which is merged. Provider selection stays in the wheel build; SGLang adds no runtime SoC detection. The residual path uses the common `torch_npu` API directly.

Vision-tower ModelSlim configuration forwarding in #36426 remains a separate change and is not included here.

After merging official main `fea48754de4b73276cad1062d6b5ae013288204d` on 2026-10-19:

items.title: [Feat] [NPU] sampling: Add sampling-mask support for Ascend
items.body:
## Motivation

Requests with `return_sampling_mask=true` are currently rejected by the Ascend sampling backend. This prevents NPU RL callers from retrieving the sampling support and behavior logprobs through the existing API.

The Ascend sampler already computes the filtered probabilities used to draw the next token. This PR exports those weights and connects them to the shared sampling-mask output pipeline, so the reported support describes the distribution used for sampling.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in `return_filtered_probs` to `top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_logits_ascend`. The fused path exports its post-top-k/top-p/min-p weights; the torch fallback scatters its filtered weights back into vocabulary order. Calls without the flag retain the tensor-only return contract.
- Pass the exported weights through `_SamplingMaskCapture` and the existing device packing and host materialization pipeline. Capture only opted-in batch rows and support both `support` and `selected` logprob modes. Support comes from positive exported weights, without replaying the filters or rewriting the sampled column.
- Remove the scheduler's Ascend-specific rejection while retaining the existing finite-top-k validation and support-cap/overflow handling. Fused cutoff ties can produce more than `top_k` candidates.
- Fix fused min-p threshold computation to use `max(dim=-1).values`.
- Add mocked fused/fallback unit coverage and an NPU HTTP test registered in `base-b-test-1-npu-a3` and `nightly-1-npu-a3`. Cover vocabulary ordering, partial-batch capture, opt-in behavior, min-p, cutoff ties, seeded mask-on/off draws, greedy sampling, restricted top-p, real fallback, and mixed output modes.

## Accuracy Tests

The following are feature-specific sampling-support and logprob correctness checks. No task-level model accuracy benchmark was run.

**Environment:** Ascend 910 A3, two dies (TP=2, EP=2), CANN 9.1, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Ascend attention/sampling backends, and DeepEP. The Qwen service was restarted from the tested checkout before the HTTP tests; NPU graph capture was enabled.

1. **Ascend capture unit tests: 9 passed, 35 deselected.**

   ```bash
   python3 -m pytest test/registered/sampling/test_sampling_mask.py \
   ```
